text:
Ibrahim Khan: hey @Brian Murphy @Amara Diallo — quick sanity check for the docs/examples refresh.

We want to lock the user-facing wording for tool-call streaming semantics (esp partial args / deltas). Can you confirm the “correct” event behavior + what we should tell customers about when it’s safe to parse args?

Also if there’s a canonical PR / acceptance test run we can link internally, drop it here.

Brian Murphy: yep. TL;DR: treat tool-call args as an *opaque string* while streaming. Don’t JSON.parse until you get the “done/completed” marker for that tool call.

More detail:
- During streaming you can receive multiple `tool_call.delta` events for the same tool call.
- The `arguments` field in deltas is a string fragment. It can be empty, and it is frequently not valid JSON until the tool call is complete.
- You should accumulate by tool call id (and index, if present) and only parse once the tool call is marked complete.

We should explicitly say “partial JSON is expected; parsing mid-stream will be flaky.”

Amara Diallo: +1. Gateway guarantees ordering per tool call:
`tool_call.delta*` → `tool_call.completed` (or equivalent “done”) → model continues

One nuance: parallel tools.
- Multiple tool calls can be in flight (distinct ids) and deltas can interleave.
- Within a single tool call id, deltas are ordered.

So the example should aggregate per-id, not “global concat”.

Dana Lo: super helpful. For TS we’re doing: map[id] += delta.arguments; only parse on completed.

Question: is the “completed” signal always emitted even if the overall stream ends early? (disconnect)

Amara Diallo: if the stream disconnects mid-flight you might never see completed. That’s one of the troubleshooting bullets IMO: “if stream ends before tool_call.completed, treat tool as not-called; retry request or resume per SDK guidance.”

Brian Murphy: yep. If the stream is cut, you can’t assume you have a valid args payload.

Docs wording suggestion (feel free to copy/paste):
“Tool arguments are streamed as UTF-8 text deltas. The payload may be incomplete or invalid JSON until the tool call is finalized. Accumulate deltas by `tool_call.id` and parse/validate only after the tool call emits a completion event.”

Sabrina James: nice. Can we also be explicit that tools are *requested* by the model, and the app decides whether to run them? (security reviewers asked)

Brian Murphy: yes please. “The model may request tools; your app must allowlist and validate args.”

github: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/18321 (Gateway validation + docs alignment for tool call streaming events)

Amara Diallo: linking acceptance run from staging from this morning. Suite: `gateway_acceptance_tool_calls_streaming`
- 148 passed, 0 failed
- includes: single tool, parallel tools, args split across 1..N deltas, and interleaving.

Also added an integration test that asserts we never emit `tool_call.completed` before the last args delta for that id.

Mateusz Zielinski: for Go, do we have a stable field list we can count on? (id/name/arguments) We’ll write aggregation against those.

Brian Murphy: stable fields:
- `tool_call.id` (string, stable)
- `tool_call.name` (string)
- `tool_call.arguments` (string; either delta fragment or final)

Index is best-effort for ordering but you should prefer id as the key.

Connor O'Brien: heads up for release notes: let’s avoid implying API behavior changed. Wording should be “clarified semantics + examples now handle partial args correctly.”

Monica Patel: +1. Thanks all. Ibrahim, can you drop the final wording into the canonical patterns doc and tag @Elliot Price / @Wei Chen to mirror it in docs?

Ibrahim Khan: will do. Action items from this thread:
- Update canonical examples to aggregate tool args by `tool_call.id`
- Only parse on `tool_call.completed` (and handle missing completed on disconnect)
- Add explicit “partial JSON is expected” note + security note (allowlist + validation)

(reactions: :thumbsup: x6)
